metaTitle: Best Shredders for Staples 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 6 best paper shredders that handle staples and paper clips, compared on sheet capacity, run time, bin size and security.
mainKeyword: shredder for staples and paper clips
summary: The Amazon Basics 15-Sheet is the best shredder for staples and paper clips, with confirmed metal handling, a P-4 cross-cut and a 20-minute run. The Bonsaii 15-Sheet is the value pick under $100, and the Aurora AU1210MA adds micro-cut security with a 60-minute run. The 8-Sheet is only for light use.
intro: A shredder that jams on the first staple is useless for real paperwork. Plenty of models claim to handle staples and clips, but the details that decide whether they cope every week, like continuous run time and a reverse function, vary widely. Metal dulls cheap cutters, and a thermal cutout that trips after three minutes makes a filing-cabinet clear-out a chore.

We ranked six shredders whose listings confirm staple or clip handling. We looked at sheet capacity, cut type, continuous run time and bin size from the spec sheets. Run time turned out to separate these machines more than sheet count, since the range runs from 3 minutes to a full 60, and a machine that stops mid-stack gets abandoned.

products.name: Amazon Basics 15-Sheet Cross Cut Paper Shredder for Home and Office
products.verdict: Confirmed staple tolerance with a long 20-minute run.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics 15-Sheet takes 15 sheets per pass with a P-4 cross-cut and an 8.7-inch entry. It handles staples, small paper clips, CDs and credit cards, runs 20 minutes continuously and has a 6-gallon bin. Run time is the spec that matters here: a shredder overheats and shuts down, so a long run means you finish a stack before it cools.

It ranks first because it doubles the Bonsaii 15-Sheet's 10 minute run and adds a larger bin, at 6 gallons against 5.5. The Aurora runs longer, but cuts only 12 sheets per pass. The tradeoff is price: it sits in the $100 to $200 bucket.

Buy it for a household with regular paperwork. The caveat is cost, and the manual feed means you stand and feed it.

products.name: Bonsaii 15-Sheet Cross Cut Paper Shredder for Home Office Heavy Duty
products.verdict: Alloy cutters and the same 15 sheets for under $100.
products.description:
The Bonsaii 15-Sheet has a P-4 cross-cut, alloy cutters and explicit handling of staples, clips, cards and CDs or DVDs. It runs 10 minutes and has a 5.5-gallon bin with a safety interlock. Alloy cutters matter because staples are hard steel, and cutter metal decides how long the blades stay sharp.

It ranks below the Amazon Basics 15-Sheet for half the run time and a smaller bin, but it costs a bracket less, in the $50 to $100 range. It also beats the Amazon Basics 12-Sheet on capacity and security level, since that model drops to P-3. The interlock stops the cutters if the bin is removed.

Buy it for staple-heavy use on a budget. The caveat is the 10 minute run time, which suits short sessions and not a full desk clear-out.
products.idealFor: Buyers shredding staples regularly on a budget.

products.name: Aurora AU1210MA Professional Grade High Security 12-Sheet Micro-Cut Shredder
products.verdict: Micro-cut security with a 60-minute run time.
products.description:
The Aurora AU1210MA is a 12-sheet P-4 micro-cut shredder that destroys CDs, credit cards and paper clips. It runs 60 minutes continuously, has a 5-gallon bin and anti-jam auto-reverse. Micro-cut produces far smaller particles than cross-cut, so shredded financial or medical records are much harder to reassemble.

It ranks third because micro-cut gives up capacity compared with the 15-sheet models, but nothing here runs longer. The hour-long run is three times the Amazon Basics 15-Sheet's 20 minutes. Against the Bonsaii 12-Sheet, it adds security and a four-fold longer run.

Buy it for sensitive documents and big batches. The caveat is the $100 to $200 price and the 12-sheet limit, which means more passes on thick stacks.

products.name: Bonsaii 12-Sheet Cross Cut Heavy Duty Paper Shredder for Home Office
products.verdict: A jam-proof reverse made for clearing staple snags.
products.description:
This Bonsaii takes 12 sheets with a P-4 cross-cut and a jam-proof reverse for clearing staple and clip snags. It runs 15 minutes, about 900 sheets per cycle, with a 5.5-gallon bin. A reverse function turns a jam from a teardown into a button press, which is how staple snags are best handled.

It ranks below the 15-sheet picks on capacity but offers a longer run than the Bonsaii 15-Sheet, 15 minutes against 10. It also lists a reverse function, which the Amazon Basics 12-Sheet does not. At $50 to $100 it costs about the same as those rivals.

Buy it if you worry about jams or clear staples constantly. The caveat is the 12-sheet limit, so thick stacks need splitting.
products.idealFor: Buyers who often hit staple jams.

products.name: Amazon Basics 12-Sheet Cross-Cut Paper and Credit Card Shredder
products.description:
The Amazon Basics 12-Sheet is a manual feed P-3 cross-cut that handles staples, small paper clips and credit cards. It runs 9 minutes and has a 5-gallon bin. P-3 is a lower security tier than P-4: its particles are bigger, so shredded text is easier to piece together.

It ranks below the Bonsaii 12-Sheet for a shorter run, 9 minutes against 15, and no stated reverse feature. It matches the Bonsaii on capacity and bracket. What it offers is the Amazon Basics name and credit card shredding, which suits households that mostly destroy junk mail.

Buy it for everyday home shredding of low-sensitivity paper. The caveat is the P-3 level, so skip it for financial or medical records.
products.skipIf: You need a higher security tier.

products.name: Amazon Basics 8-Sheet High Security Cross Cut Paper and Credit Card Shredder
products.verdict: The cheapest way to get confirmed staple tolerance.
products.description:
The Amazon Basics 8-Sheet is a P-4 cross-cut with 5x18mm particles that handles staples, small paper clips and credit cards. It runs 3 minutes and has a 3.7-gallon bin. Fine 5x18mm particles give it better security than the P-3 12-Sheet despite the lower price.

It ranks last for low capacity and short run, but it is the lowest priced pick at $25 to $50 and the only compact one. Three minutes means it stops mid-stack, and a 3.7-gallon bin fills fast. The Bonsaii 15-Sheet costs more but runs more than three times longer.

Buy it for light use, like a few pages and the occasional card. The caveat is endurance: do not plan to clear a filing cabinet with it.
products.idealFor: Light shredding on a tight budget.

whatMatters.detail: Staple and clip tolerance means the cutters are built to chew metal without jamming or dulling. Cheap shredders often fail here. Look for the exact words staples and paper clips in the specs, not just heavy duty. The Amazon Basics 15-Sheet and Bonsaii 15-Sheet both state it. Remove large binder clips first.

Continuous run time is how long the shredder works before its motor needs a cooldown. A 3-minute model stalls on a pile, while the Aurora runs 60 minutes. Look for the number of minutes in the specs and match it to the biggest stack you shred in one sitting. Long sessions need long run times, so do not buy on sheet capacity alone.

P-3, P-4 and micro-cut describe particle size. Higher means finer pieces and better protection for sensitive papers. P-4 and micro-cut suit bank statements and medical records. Look for the P rating or particle size, such as the 5x18mm on the Amazon Basics 8-Sheet. P-3 is fine for junk mail.

Bin size controls how often you empty the shredder. A small bin, like the 3.7 gallons on the Amazon Basics 8-Sheet, fills fast with a stack. A 5.5 or 6-gallon bin lasts longer. Check the gallons on the listing and consider how much paper you shred in a typical session and how often you are willing to empty it.

A reverse function backs paper and staples out of the cutters when something jams. It turns a jam into a button press and not a teardown. The Bonsaii 12-Sheet lists a jam-proof reverse and the Aurora an anti-jam auto-reverse. Look for reverse or anti-jam in the features and note whether it is automatic or button-driven, since the first clears a snag without your help.

faq.a: Yes, each listing confirms staple or small paper clip handling. Remove large binder clips first. The Amazon Basics 15-Sheet and Bonsaii 15-Sheet are explicit about staples and small clips, and neither promises to take heavy-duty clamps.

faq.q: What is the biggest buying mistake?
faq.a: Ignoring run time. A shredder that stops after 3 minutes, like the Amazon Basics 8-Sheet, frustrates anyone with a stack. The Aurora runs 60 minutes, so match the cooldown to your habits.

faq.q: Is the Aurora worth it over the Amazon Basics 15-Sheet?
faq.a: If you want micro-cut security and a 60 minute run, yes. The Aurora cuts 12 sheets, though, and the Amazon Basics 15-Sheet holds more per pass, so thick stacks go slower. Choose by sensitivity versus capacity, and by how long your sessions run.

faq.q: How do I clear a jam?
faq.a: Use the reverse function, then feed fewer sheets. The Bonsaii 12-Sheet has a jam-proof reverse for staple snags, and the Aurora reverses automatically. Unplug before reaching into the feed, and clear the cutters of any torn paper.

The Amazon Basics models list credit card handling, as does the Aurora, which destroys cards and CDs. Feed cards one at a time unless the manual says otherwise, and check each model's manual for card limits and any slot that is meant for cards.

faq.q: Why is the Bonsaii 15 Sheet cheaper?
faq.a: It sits in the $50 to $100 bucket with a 10 minute run time, against the Amazon Basics 15-Sheet's $100 to $200 and 20 minutes. The Bonsaii gives alloy cutters, but a smaller bin and a shorter run, which is the price of the lower bracket.

finalTake: Buy the Amazon Basics 15-Sheet for regular household paperwork and the longest practical sessions. Choose the Bonsaii 15-Sheet when budget matters, and the Aurora when documents are sensitive or you shred in long batches. Skip the 8-Sheet unless you shred a few pages a week.
